stories.title: Jehoshaphat's Prayer
stories.passageSummary: It comes to pass that the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them other beside the Ammonites, come against Jehoshaphat to battle. There come some that tell Jehoshaphat: There cometh a great multitude against thee from beyond the sea on this side Syria; and, behold, they be in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi. Jehoshaphat fears, and sets himself to seek the LORD, and proclaims a fast throughout all Judah. Judah gathers themselves together, to ask help of the LORD: even out of all the cities of Judah they come to seek the LORD. Jehoshaphat stands in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court, and says: O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee? Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever? And they dwelt therein, and have built thee a sanctuary therein for thy name, saying: If, when evil cometh upon us, as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help. And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not; behold, I say, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit. O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee. All Judah stands before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children. Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah comes the Spirit of the LORD in the midst of the congregation, and he says: Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the LORD unto you: Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's. Tomorrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel. Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Fear not, nor be dismayed; tomorrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you. Jehoshaphat bows his head with his face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fall before the LORD, worshipping the LORD. The Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stand up to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

stories.title: What God Hath Cleansed
stories.passageSummary: On the morrow, as they go on their journey, and draw nigh unto the city, Peter goes up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour. He becomes very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he falls into a trance, and sees heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air. And there comes a voice to him: Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. Peter says: Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. The voice speaks unto him again the second time: What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. This is done thrice: and the vessel is received up again into heaven. While Peter doubts in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean, behold, the men which were sent from Cornelius have made enquiry for Simon's house, and stand before the gate, and call, and ask whether Simon, which is surnamed Peter, were lodged there. While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit says unto him: Behold, three men seek thee. Arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them. Peter goes down to the men which are sent unto him from Cornelius, and says: Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come? They say: Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by an holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words of thee. Then he calls them in, and lodges them. On the morrow Peter goes away with them, and certain brethren from Joppa accompany him.

stories.title: I Will Lift Up Mine Eyes
stories.passageSummary: A Song of degrees. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore. Render as the psalm being sung aloud — observable scene of a pilgrim on the road to Jerusalem singing this song of ascent, or a gathering of pilgrims singing it together as they climb. Hills visible. Road dust on the feet. Keep it observable, not abstract.

stories.title: Today Shalt Thou Be with Me in Paradise
stories.passageSummary: One of the malefactors which were hanged with Jesus rails on him, saying: If thou be Christ, save thyself and us. But the other answering rebukes him, saying: Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss. He says unto Jesus: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. Jesus says unto him: Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

stories.title: As for Me and My House
stories.passageSummary: Joshua addresses all the tribes of Israel gathered at Shechem. Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD. And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. The people answer and say: God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; for the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and which did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way wherein we went, and among all the people through whom we passed: and the LORD drove out from before us all the people, even the Amorites which dwelt in the land: therefore will we also serve the LORD; for he is our God.
